title: Kumbalanga Pulissery
name: Kumbalanga Pulissery (Ash Gourd Mor Curry)
subtitle: Kerala's Onam sadya favourite — tender ash gourd in a coconut-spiced curd curry.
protein: ~5–6g protein per adult serving — from curd

method.title: Cook the ash gourd
items: Cook on medium until just soft — ash gourd cooks fast, so don't overcook it
Turn the flame to the lowest setting

method.label: Toddler — her bowl (before the chili paste)
items: Scoop {=2–3 tbsp} of the soft ash gourd into her bowl and mash lightly
Stir in {@curd:toddler} and {@coconut:toddler} — a mild coconut-curd for her

method.title: Grind and add the curd
items: Drain {@rice|the soaked rice}; grind it with {@coconut:main}, {@green-chili}, {@red-chili} and {@cumin} to a nice smooth paste
Whisk {@curd:main} in a bowl and stir in the ground paste
Pour this spiced mixture into the cooked ash gourd and stir well; adjust the salt
Keep on medium flame, stirring continuously for the first 3–4 min so it doesn't split
When a frothy layer forms on top, switch off — don't let it boil, or it turns watery

method.title: Temper and serve
items: In a separate pan, heat {@coconut-oil}; add {@mustard} and let them splutter
Add {@methi}, {@red-chilies} and {@curry-leaves}; fry a few seconds
Add {@hing} and pour the seasoning over the pulissery
Best eaten hot, alongside plain steamed rice

method.label: Tip
method.text: Cucumber works in place of ash gourd. Keep the fenugreek to ¼ tsp even in a bigger batch — more makes the curry bitter. Slightly sour curd gives the best flavour. Hing was added to the tempering. Stovetop in a heavy pan — curd needs gentle, watched heat so it doesn't split.
